authoritative_for: Decisions owns its durable runs, observations, admitted candidates, normalized candidate meaning, source anchors, append-only reviews, lifecycle-event order and envelopes, daily projections and snapshots, and delivery attempts.
Decisions SQLite is authoritative for those records and their domain transitions.
not_authoritative_for: Only the cited user message supplies decision authority; file activity selects an enacted turn but does not make a decision.

Conversations owns normalized conversation-source resolution, Nucleus owns bounded execution and retained request and output records, Email owns transport acceptance, and lifecycle consumers own their copied state, cursor, policy, retry, retention, and domain success.

covers: All supported public Decisions CLI outcomes, supported local-product consumer surfaces, installation and recovery operations, and development operations in this release.
excludes: Help and version display, implementation primitives, direct SQLite access, upstream product capabilities, client-side hook trust, current runtime readiness, and downstream consumer behavior are outside this inventory claim.

shared_access_and_trust: Decisions interfaces are local-user surfaces; each entry separately declares whether it reads, writes, or invokes another product.
A published read surface does not authorize direct SQLite access, mutation through that surface, or downstream interpretation as Decisions authority.
shared_privacy_and_retention: Decisions state is private local-user state and may contain normalized decision text and machine-local source anchors.
A capability may disclose or invoke another product only where its own entry explicitly says so; no general disclosure or retention promise follows from provider installation.
compatibility_and_retirement: Provider release identifies these exact bundle bytes, and entry contract versions identify documented semantic compatibility.
No additional cross-release support, migration window, or deprecation period is promised unless an entry declares it.
operational_limits: Inventory completeness concerns published interfaces and operations, not live service readiness, downstream availability, or unlimited throughput and retention.
Per-entry contracts own command bounds, failure behavior, recovery, and any narrower non-guarantees.
